production_metadata.production_description: The trureturning formalization campaign. Human direction selected the benchmark, campaign objective and submission identity; mathematical proof implementation used Codex CLI. Independent mathematical/source review passed with two Codex CLI seats and one GPT-6 Pro seat through the chrono-500 pool; the CLI tests seat freshly recompiled all seven candidate modules and the untouched official Solution. This is an attributed formalization of Giles Gardam's known counterexample, not a claim of a new mathematical counterexample. It builds on Gardam's paper (arXiv:2102.11818v2, sections 3.1–3.2) and pinned Mathlib APIs. The proof supplies a faithful two-sided normal-form equivalence for the exact PresentedGroup, torsion-freeness, explicit two-sided inverse identities, and group-ring support and transport arguments. It locally compiled with the benchmark's Lean 4.35.0-rc3 / Mathlib 5e0c4e5239cb0a2d86d68a884bf52cfd963fce22 pins, with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound in the printed transitive axiom closures. No manual human proof edits are reported. Allowed LeanPool Polylean related machinery was discovered separately after this candidate was produced; it is not imported by the submitted proof. Official comparator and nanoda acceptance are requested and not presumed from local compilation. No measured monetary-cost claim is made.

The trureturing formalization campaign (Claude orchestration; Codex CLI implementation; independent Codex CLI and Claude review). The core mathematics is reused, not original: the stronger Park–Pham (Kahn–Kalai) bound is taken from the public, sorry-free Lean Pool theorem `KahnKalai.park_pham_bound` (`LeanPool/KahnKalai`, Apache-2.0, by Dan Clemens Posch, upstream https://github.com/dcposch/kahn-kalai-lean, following arXiv:2303.02144), imported from the benchmark-pinned lean-pool `e9d53e9cbcff8dfd0cc816ba94db7a26b082929f` as allowed for solutions. This submission adds the transport to the benchmark statement of Frankston–Kahn–Narayanan–Park (universe change to `Fin n`, minimal elements and the bound by `l`, `setBernoulli` = explicit product measure, monotonicity of the Bernoulli measure of an upper family, comparison of `p_c` with the pool threshold, integral covers as fractional covers, log₂→ln with `K = 100000 / log 2`). Locally (Lean 4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 5e0c4e5239cb0a2d86d68a884bf52cfd963fce22) Submission, the trusted Solution and Challenge compile, and `theorem_1_1` and `K` print only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Official comparator and nanoda acceptance are requested, not presumed. No measured monetary-cost claim is made.

The trureturing formalization campaign (Claude orchestration; Codex CLI implementation; independent Codex CLI and Claude review). The mathematical content is reused, not original: both holes are obtained from the public, sorry-free Lean Pool theorem `Mathoverflow1973.SixSphereComplexAtlas.exists_complex_analytic_atlas` (`LeanPool/HopfProblem`, Apache-2.0, by Boris Alexeev, formalizing the construction claimed by Alpöge 2026), imported from the benchmark-pinned lean-pool `e9d53e9cbcff8dfd0cc816ba94db7a26b082929f` as allowed for solutions. This submission adds only a model-space transport from `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)` to `Fin 3 → ℂ` along `EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin 3) ℂ`; the generic transport code is adapted (with attribution) from Lean Pool `LeanPool/HopfProblem/Threefold/SpecialPeriods7.lean`. Locally (Lean 4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 5e0c4e5239cb0a2d86d68a884bf52cfd963fce22) Submission, the trusted Solution and Challenge compile and both holes print only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Official comparator and nanoda acceptance are requested, not presumed. No measured monetary-cost claim is made.

The trureturning formalization campaign. Human direction selected the benchmark, submission identity and public-source reuse policy. Codex performed source-closure packaging, import remapping and local Lean verification. This submission reuses the complete public Apache-2.0 formalization of `DifferentialGeometry.Topology.poincare_high_dim_topological` from https://github.com/qinz1yang/differential-geometry at commit `788efe97894474c032de6dfb1289d515f613d15a`; original full-proof authorship and new mathematical discovery are not claimed. The 237-module reachable closure is placed under `Submission/DifferentialGeometry/`, preserving original namespaces, proof bodies and headers while prefixing local imports. The root proof applies the existing theorem to the exact official revision-1 telescope.

The source snapshot contains exactly one workspace, for `poincare_high_dim_topological`. The official Challenge, Solution, WorkspaceTest, configuration, toolchain and dependency declarations are unchanged. The candidate compiled with Lean v4.35.0-rc3 and Mathlib `5e0c4e5239cb0a2d86d68a884bf52cfd963fce22`; `lake build Submission` and `lake build Solution` passed. The theorem's printed transitive axiom closure contains only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. All 240 overlaid Lean files were byte-compared against the locally verified workspace. Full upstream LICENSE, NOTICE and source provenance are additionally retained as comments in `Submission/Attribution/UpstreamLicense.lean` so the evaluated source-only overlay preserves them. No additional Lake dependency is requested.

Local compilation is not an organizer acceptance claim. Local `lake test` could not launch because comparator/Nanoda are not installed on this host; official comparator and mandatory Nanoda verification are requested. This is an additional total-only submission; earlier accepted results by other teams are acknowledged. No measured monetary-cost or independent GPT Pro review claim is made.

The trureturing formalization campaign (Claude orchestration; Codex CLI implementation; independent Codex CLI and Claude review). The core mathematics is reused, not original: Szemerédi's theorem in finite form (`Combinatorics.ArithmeticProgression.exists_of_density_nat_atTop`) comes from Gabriel Dahia's density Hales–Jewett formalization (https://github.com/gdahia/densityhalesjewett), as packaged in Lean Pool `LeanPool/DensityHalesJewett` at lean-pool `5e0b39aee56fe9e23bae9bed852a42fef9260b92` (Apache-2.0). Because that project is newer than the benchmark-pinned lean-pool, its 14 files are vendored under `Submission/DHJ/` (module renames, one provenance line per file, and explicit binders `θ κ` added to one `variable` line in `Subspace.lean` so the code builds under the workspace's `autoImplicit = false`; see NOTICE.md). This submission adds only the bridge from the finite statement to the benchmark's positive-upper-density formulation. Locally (Lean 4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 5e0c4e5239cb0a2d86d68a884bf52cfd963fce22) all Submission files, the trusted Solution and Challenge compile with `-DautoImplicit=false`, and `szemeredi` prints only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. This resubmission fixes the build failure of #1966. Official comparator and nanoda acceptance are requested, not presumed. No measured monetary-cost claim is made.

The trureturing formalization campaign (Claude orchestration; Codex CLI implementation; independent Codex CLI and Claude review). The mathematics is reused, not original: the bound 246 is `bombieriVinogradov_implies_prime_gap_le_246` from AxiomMath/PrimeGapsLib (1faa7b14), made unconditional by the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem of kimihiro64/bombieri-vinogradov (7a174830), with dependencies kimihiro64/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd (0f15a38c) and kimihiro64/Robin1984 (bfa72aec), all Apache-2.0. These are vendored under `Submission/` with renamed modules, Lean 4.35 / Mathlib API ports, per-file provenance and modification notices (see NOTICE.md); the PrimeGapsLib numerical certificate is embedded byte-for-byte as a Lean string and is still checked by the kernel. This submission adds only the vendoring, the ports and the final bridge. Locally, in a clean copy of the generated workspace containing only the submitted .lean files, all 1,282 Submission modules, Submission, the trusted Solution and Challenge compile with `-DautoImplicit=false` (Lean 4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 5e0c4e5239cb0a2d86d68a884bf52cfd963fce22), and the hole prints only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Serial local compile time of the closure is about 70 minutes. Official comparator and nanoda acceptance are requested, not presumed. No measured monetary-cost claim is made.
